body:
Three risks, three states of repair

Carousel No. 25, September 15th, 2026

Shipped at 7.578

renderWARN — 9 slide(s), 39 overflow warning(s)
qaWARN — 0 fail(s), 42 warn(s)
aggregatesPASS — 10 declaration(s), 13 numeric phrase(s) in the render, all re-derived
assemblyPASS — 9 slide(s), 9.27 MB, vector

numeralsPASS — 19 numeral(s) over 9 frame(s), every one reachable

What degraded

  • The Bottleneck Scanner's daily ceiling was not checked. No Supabase connector is available in this session, so the query could not be run at all. Nobody looked at the scan cap or the 24 hour failure count today.
  • Five of the six research scouts died on a weekly model rate limit and were re-spawned on a smaller model to protect the quota. The findings they returned were fact-checked the same way.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Three risks, three states of repair, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

The problem is not the megawatts.

ERCOT's board just heard that the real risk is speed. Large Loads tied to AI training can swing fast enough to strain a generator's shaft and potentially damage it. The draft rule would cap that swing at 10 MW per 5 seconds.

A ride through rule took effect August 1st. A better modeling rule reaches the Board this month. That swing rule itself has no number yet. What it has is a plan to file it in September or October.

Six pages name no data center, no company and no generator. ERCOT also says its own models are too inaccurate to study these loads' grid impact, so it went to Texas A&M for a new one.

How much of that swing still runs on a model ERCOT calls inadequate?

#ERCOT #PUCT #LargeLoads

2. The first comment

Sources, two official records, all fetched September 15th.

The machine changed itself

  • scripts/carousel/copy_sync_check.py gains banned_characters(): every em dash, en dash, curly quote and emoji in copy.json AND in the render's text nodes is a hard fail, with the character, the surface and the string named.
    CLAUDE.md bans those characters ANYWHERE and no gate had ever read a slide for them.
  • scripts/carousel/ledger_check.py gains misfiled_median(): an artwork.json entry that carries a NUMBER under a key reducing to the same shape as deck_median_L, and no deck_median_L, is reported as a MISFILING by name rather than folded into the 'predates the measurement' note.
    check_register counts the light deck cap off value.deck_median_L, because that figure is measured off the shipped render rather than asserted by a run about itself.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

VERIFIED. The 2026-09-15 worklist re-fetched, 12 urls over 10 bodies. One claim moved rather than dropped: tx-2026-0109-c7 cited the Legislature's upcoming-meetings page, which carries only what is still ahead, so the canceled September 3rd sitting had come off it. It now cites the committee's own meetings archive, which still marks that row canceled. ADMITTED. Three, led by ERCOT's own Large Load risk list for its Board of Directors (tx-2026-0159), plus UT Physicians ambient listening in Harris (tx-2026-0160) and UT Arlington's AI tutor with Fort Worth PD in Tarrant (tx-2026-0161). The record stands at 138 items and 762 claims, backlog 0. HELD. Nothing. Twelve candidate claims were rejected during verification and four absences were registered instead, each naming the document it is absent from. THE DECK. Carousel no. 25, scored 7.578 by three judges against a 6.7 bar, spread 0.05, no hard fail on any card. Zero QA fails across nine frames. WHAT THE RUN LEARNED ABOUT ITSELF. The value arc was rewritten rather than redrawn, off a measurement: on this deck's dark ground a white field through the stipple prints at a mean of 63.0 of 255, a ceiling of L* 26.7, and the plan had asked a stipple frame for 40. Frame 3 was rebuilt for the other reason, a wall buried under the type's own scrim. The pixel round found seven defects no gate saw, including two furniture lines printing through each other, an en dash in the deck's own furniture, a bearing pedestal drawn entirely below the frame and a declared straightedge never drawn. numeral_lint stopped the site build on the claim count 44, which had passed until today by collision. house_style_check found 18 sentences over the 30 word backstop in copy this run wrote. CI caught the one thing no local run could: the record grew a date kind this morning that had no English label. NOTHING PROMPTED. prompt_audit measured 1336 tool calls and none waited on a human. THE REVIEW. An automated reviewer read the pull request and returned 12 findings. 11 were acted on before the merge and every one was verified against the stored quote first. Three narrowed the record to what its own evidence supports. tx-2026-0161 said police testing had begun where the quote says the researchers are helping to develop the training. tx-2026-0160 said one system for every doctor where the quote says a unified system. tx-2026-0159 carried an effective key date of 2026-08-01 when the source says August 1 with NO YEAR and the claim's own note forbids adding one downstream, so that date is gone. Two fixed how the record describes itself. tx-2026-0159's public access room said open_meeting, which makes the site advertise a way to take part in a rule that cannot be commented on until it is filed. It is contact_only now, and the how text says what a reader can and cannot do. tx-2026-0161's key date was typed as decided when it is the day the university published its account. Three made the shipped computation rerunnable by somebody else. compute.py held the container's own home directory as a constant and its extraction of the source lived only in gitignored scratch, so a fresh checkout could not recompute a single figure. Both are fixed, the extractions are committed beside the run, and the archived update_ledgers.py counted one directory too few for where it is archived. One was the gate table disagreeing with the artifact it certifies. gate_status counted the caption with str.split, which is 138 whitespace tokens including three hashtags, and caption_check counts 139 the way the comma ceiling will be computed. It asks caption_check now.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
